title: Facing down a gangster with Lester Young
summary: He and Lester walk out on a gangster's demand to keep playing.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Speaking of ---------- incident...you told me when we were talking over the phone that there was some incident involving you and Lester Young...that you...

Oh. I was considered...well not...I was a piano player, but I wasn't considered one. So this night they needed somebody to play with him...with Lester and some other musicians. So the man said we went to work at 9 o'clock and you quit at 3. And in those days, everybody knew that I was from Texas and the people supposed to have a gun. So after we played all night...people liked it...and at 3 o'clock Lester and I started to pack up, leave...this person supposed to / a gangster came have been

and said, "Get back on that stand." And I put my coat on, and then I said to Lester...Lester got his horn and I got my gun out and put it under my coat and said, "Let's go." We walked out. And the musicians are still wondering how we didn't get killed, you know, defying the guy. But that's exactly what happened. He said, "Get back on that stand." And I said, "Shit, (you know) you got to be kidding." I said, "I wonder if he know who he's talking to." The other guy...all the musicians standing there playing like hell. (Laughter). Yep, they stayed and played. That was in 1926...I said I was working with Mrs. Moore, you know what I mean. When we went up to (Ardmore?) and saw...I was just checking to see if some of those things were right, you know. And they're pretty accurate.
